dedupe_keys.name: numerical modelling of an oil sands tailings dam breach runout and overland flow mahdi shakibaeinia and dibike 2020

description: This case study models the consequences of a hypothetical breach of an oil-sands tailings dam in Alberta, Canada, simulating the runout and non-Newtonian overland flow of the released tailings, the resulting flooding, and the spill into nearby water bodies. It was carried out by Abdellah Mahdi and Ahmad Shakibaeinia of Polytechnique Montreal with Yonas Dibike of Environment and Climate Change Canada and published in Science of the Total Environment in 2020. The dam-breach model uses a visco-plastic rheology and was first validated on the 2014 Mount Polley tailings dam breach in British Columbia, where it reproduced the flooding extent and the water level wave in a downstream lake. The study is site scale. The article is paywalled at Elsevier under Crown Copyright, with a free author copy hosted by the University of Northern British Columbia. Findings: about half of the tailings deposit overland and the rest reaches the Lower Athabasca River, and treating tailings as non-Newtonian doubles flood travel time and slightly reduces the spill compared with water. Caveats: results are highly sensitive to viscosity and yield stress, which need calibration, and the scenario is hypothetical. For simulation it shows how to set up and validate tailings runout models for hazard exposure and emergency response planning around mine waste facilities. It is related to the Mount Polley tailings breach review and the tailings dam breach runout characteristics records in this catalogue.
